predecessors.name: First French Empire
predecessors.text: the former Duchy of Luxembourg, 'restored' by the Congress of Vienna after Napoleon's defeat and raised to a Grand Duchy

ledger.x: 1815: the Congress of Vienna creates the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
1815: Prussia receives the north-eastern Eifel part of the duchy.
1830: the Belgian revolt takes most of the Grand Duchy.
1839: the German-speaking rump returns to the Grand Duke.
1890: the personal union with the Netherlands ends and a new dynasty takes the throne.
2 August 1914: Germany occupies Luxembourg without a fight.
22 November 1918: the last German troops leave.
10 September 1944: American troops liberate Luxembourg City.

wars.name: Belgian Revolution
wars.outcome: Belgium took most of the Grand Duchy in 1830; the Treaty of London (1839) gave Belgium 4,730 km2 (65%) and left the German-speaking rump to the Grand Duke.

wars.name: German invasion of Luxembourg in World War I
wars.outcome: Occupation from 2 August to 22 November 1918 with Luxembourg's government kept; no change of frontier.

wars.name: German invasion of Luxembourg in World War II
wars.outcome: Occupied from 10 May 1940 and annexed to Gau Moselland; liberated from 9 September 1944, with the Ardennes offensive delaying the end to early 1945.

certainty.note: The Grand Duchy's frontier with the Netherlands' southern provinces and the Belgian rebels was disputed after 1830; the 1815 line is a Congress of Vienna line.
Treaty frontiers: the Treaty of London of 1839, confirmed by the Second Treaty of London in 1867; the 1919 and 1945 frontiers are unchanged.
